turtle.kaynak: Curtis Faith, Way of the Turtle (System 1: 20-day, System 2: 55-day breakouts)
turtle.nedir: A daily close above the highest high (or below the lowest low) of the last 20 or 55 days. The Turtles bought the first and shorted the second, and rode the trend.
turtle.zayif: Most breakouts fail: in sideways markets it takes many small losses; the profit comes from a few long trends.

rsi2.kaynak: Larry Connors & Cesar Alvarez, Short Term Trading Strategies That Work
rsi2.nedir: A sharp 2-day pullback inside the long-term trend: close above the 200-day average with RSI(2) under 5 (long), or below it with RSI(2) over 95 (short). Exit when the close crosses the 5-day average.
rsi2.zayif: Wins often but small; the book uses no stop, so one market that keeps falling can wipe out many small gains. Tested on stocks, not crypto.

trend.nedir: Four moving-average crossovers, each scaled by the market's own volatility and combined into one number from −20 (strong downtrend) to +20 (strong uptrend). 0 = no trend.
trend.zayif: Late at turning points by design: it follows, it does not predict. Small accounts pay a lot in fees if they trade every change.

kalabalik.kaynak: Squeeze research note perp/27: funding + open interest (trader-hafiza)
kalabalik.nedir: Over the last 24 h one side paid funding while open interest rose more than 5%: more traders piled into the side that already pays. Crowded shorts are the classic short-squeeze fuel.
kalabalik.zayif: Crowded can stay crowded for days; it says where the pressure is, not when it releases. Needs our own hourly snapshots, so some markets show no reading.
